                                 SUMMARY OF RESPONSIVE TESTIMONY


                                                         Of

                                                  Frank Mossburg

                The purpose of my testimony is to review OG&E’s request for relief in this docket. This
         includes the approval of three Electric Service Agreements (ESAs) with Google as the ultimate
         customer and two Capacity Purchase Agreements (CPAs).
                The CPAs are provided by Google as part of the transaction. These cover the purchase of
         capacity from two new solar facilities. This is meant to, in part, cover for the needs generated by
         the new ESAs.
                OG&E is requesting pre-approval of the CPAs under 17 OS 286c. Under this statute the
         Commission must find that there is a need for the resource and that there has been a
         consideration of reasonable alternatives.

                I have come to the following conclusions:

                            •   OG&E demonstrates a need for new generation supply.

                            •   The CPAs feature standard contractual protections, are priced lower than
                                recent market transactions, and appear to be a unique opportunity.

                            •   The ESAs feature reasonable protections for ratepayers.

                            •   While the CPAs cover a portion of the future need, additional procurement
                                would be needed if load appears as projected in the ESAs. Therefore care
                                must be taken during actual rate setting to assure cost shifts do not impact
                                residential ratepayers.

                            •   The Commission should act to establish guidelines for a process by which
                                the impact of adding this new load will be determined to avoid future
                                disputes.
